job.title: Jobs
job.subtitle: Work conditions, hiring
job.pageSubtitle: Check the work conditions for your visa status.

partTimeConditionDesc.D2: Students need a part-time work permit in advance, and the allowed hours differ between semester and vacation periods. Check the exact conditions with your school's international office or your local immigration office.
partTimeConditionDesc.D4: Language students need to meet requirements like attendance rate and Korean proficiency before getting a part-time work permit. Check the exact conditions with your school's international office or your local immigration office.
partTimeConditionDesc.H1: Working Holiday status generally allows a wider range of work, but some industries may be restricted. Check the exact scope on HiKorea.
partTimeConditionDesc.F2: Residence status generally has fewer work restrictions than other visa types, but the details can vary by individual case. Check with HiKorea for specifics.
partTimeConditionDesc.F5: Permanent Residence status has very few work restrictions, though some industries may require separate qualifications. Check with HiKorea for specifics.
partTimeConditionDesc.F6: Marriage Migrant status generally has fewer work restrictions, but the details can vary by individual case. Check with HiKorea for specifics.
partTimeConditionDesc.DEFAULT: Whether a part-time work permit is required, and the allowed scope of work, varies significantly by visa status. Check with your local immigration office or HiKorea for the exact conditions.

job.stayExpirationDays: {{days}} days until expiration. Planning your extension timing in advance also helps with planning your work schedule.
job.stayExpirationClose: Your stay period is expiring soon. It's a good idea to recheck your extension status along with your part-time work permit.
job.stayExpirationExpired: Check your stay status first — sorting that out matters more than checking work conditions right now.
job.stayExpirationUnknown: No stay expiration date on file. Add it in Edit Profile for more accurate guidance.
job.howToCheckDesc: You can check the exact work conditions and procedures for your visa status at your school's international office or student support center, HiKorea, your local immigration office, or Worknet (Ministry of Employment and Labor).

simulation.subtitle: Pick your options and enter the amounts you know
simulation.inputHint: Leave a field empty to use the average value
simulation.resultDescription: Here is the estimated cost breakdown based on your selections.
simulation.disclaimer: * This is an estimate. Actual costs vary by school, district, and lifestyle.
simulation.depositNote: The deposit ({{amount}}) is refunded when you move out, so it is excluded from the monthly budget.
simulation.suppliesNote: Household supplies (detergent, tissue, toiletries) vary too much per person to estimate, so they are not included. Setting aside 30,000-70,000 KRW a month is a good rule of thumb.

transport.kpassPromo: K-Pass refunds part of your fare when you take public transit 15+ times a month — 20% for everyone, up to 30% if you are aged 19-34. Well worth applying for if you commute often.

partTimePermit.title: Part-Time Work Permit
partTimePermit.reasonWorking: Your profile says you are currently working part-time. Please double-check that you have received a part-time work permit.
partTimePermit.reasonSearching: If you are looking for a part-time job, you must obtain a part-time work permit before you start working.
partTimePermit.target: International students who want to work part-time on a {{visaType}} status
partTimePermit.situation: A holder of a study-purpose status wants to engage in work outside their designated activity
partTimePermit.action: Apply in advance for a part-time work activity permit at your local immigration office.
partTimePermit.details: Permitted hours differ during the semester and during vacation, and some industries are restricted. Check the exact conditions with your university's international office or on HiKorea.
